facts.F245: An operator whom the Invite a member or Machine tokens page would refuse does not see that item anywhere in the nav, at desk width and at phone width, open or folded.
facts.F246: The oracle sees only the nav states it opened; a hidden item that appears in a fold, a sub menu, or at another width it did not open stays unobserved, and absence in one capture cannot prove absence for every refused operator.
facts.F247: The promise does not say whether the item must be absent or only inactive; the observation must show absence from the operator's view, not merely a disabled look.
facts.F248: At desk width, on a page taller than the window, the operator scrolls the page to the bottom and the whole nav, from its first item to its last, is still in view; this holds with the nav open and with the nav folded.

facts.F251: At 480 px wide and below, the nav bar above the content takes no more than a fifth of the screen height, measured while the operator looks at a normal page.

facts.F253: The promise does not say whether 'screen height' is the whole screen or the browser view, so the observation must state what it measured against.

facts.F255: Counting the links in the bar does not show that the operator can press them; items pushed out of sight by horizontal overflow, or covered by the content, stay unobserved unless each one is really pressed and the page it opens is seen.
facts.F256: The promise does not list the destinations, so the observation must name the full set it pressed.
facts.F257: In the nav's lower group, Sign out and the theme control look as quiet as the other items beside them: neither one stands out as the heaviest thing in the nav, for example as a filled or coloured button among plain items.
facts.F258: Quietness is a matter of how the nav looks to the operator; a check of style names or classes does not show the seen weight, and a single screenshot cannot show the look in the other theme, on hover, or at phone width.
facts.F259: The promise gives no measurable test for 'quiet' or 'heaviest', so the observation must be a visible comparison with the neighbouring items, and the examiner must say where the judgment is a matter of degree.

facts.F261: The oracle sees the single press it made; it does not see whether the theme choice holds after she loads another page or comes back later, and a sign out that appears to work can still leave the old session usable.

facts.F27: L1 to L2, in crates/foundry-app/src/admin_tokens.rs: the four renders at 70, 107, 170 and 393 each assemble the rail with the same five arguments. Then the follow-up change names the new section ONCE instead of four times, so three of the four sites cannot be forgotten.
facts.F270: The operator sees only the places she can go, and everything the nav shows her opens when she presses it.
facts.F271: The two links are hidden from an operator they would refuse by a different means than her rights, for instance by the page she happens to be on; the four rights rows are driven on one and the same page, so only a rights-shaped cause satisfies all four.

facts.F274: What the nav no longer shows her is also still closed to her, and the application tells her nothing about what exists behind it.
